QUIC drop test with client and server fibres, packet loss emulation, and stream send/receive checks.

# Purpose
This file is a QUIC integration test that runs a client and a server in the same process by using `fd_fibre` scheduling and a virtual network pair. It creates two `fd_quic_t` instances, one with the `FD_QUIC_ROLE_CLIENT` role and one with the `FD_QUIC_ROLE_SERVER` role, then connects them through `fd_quic_virtual_pair_t` and `fd_quic_netem_t` objects to simulate packet loss and network delay. The test drives both endpoints with a shared test clock, services each QUIC state machine, and uses callbacks such as [`my_handshake_complete`](<#my_handshake_complete>), [`my_connection_new`](<#my_connection_new>), [`my_stream_rx_cb`](<#my_stream_rx_cb>), and [`my_cb_conn_final`](<#my_cb_conn_final>) to track handshake completion, stream reception, and connection finalization.

The main test logic sends `NUM_STREAMS` stream messages from the client to the server, checks that received data matches the send count, and periodically closes and reopens connections after batches of sends. The server fibre only services incoming traffic and waits until `server_done` is set. The file also sets up workspace memory, RNG state, QUIC limits, and cleanup code for all allocated objects. In effect, this file verifies QUIC connection setup, stream creation, stream send and receive, connection close, and callback handling under a controlled simulated network.
